name: Samsøe Samsøe
why: Copenhagen's accessible contemporary house — utilitarian street ease in a muted palette, priced to be worn rather than saved.
origin: Klaus and Preben Samsøe, Copenhagen's Latin Quarter, 1993 — a jewellery shop that grew into men's tees and knitwear, sold on in 2000 and built into an international house.
opview: The house describes its own look as Copenhagen street utility carried in a Scandinavian spirit — minimal, affordable, meant to outlast the season.

onething.n: the category the house grew out of jewellery to make, and still the clearest statement of the register. NO LINK — no US-facing product page verified in this pass

notes.scandi: the register is the entire proposition, and the house says so in its own words rather than leaving it to be read
notes.style: muted palette and utilitarian silhouettes carried consistently rather than reinvented seasonally
notes.reach: large in Northern Europe, thin in the US, where it arrives through specialty shops

cities: Own stores across Denmark and Europe including Copenhagen, London and Brussels; US reach through specialty independents
